module_title: Inner vs. Outer Planets, Asteroids, and Earth's Chemical Composition
introduction: At this level, we will categorize the planets into Terrestrial and Jovian groups, identify the rocky boundary between Mars and Jupiter, and analyze the layers of the Earth based on their dominant chemical elements (SIAL, SIMA, NIFE).

core_concepts.title: Terrestrial (Inner) Planets
core_concepts.description: The first 4 planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are called 'Inner or Terrestrial' planets. They are made up of dense rocks and metals, have solid surfaces, and possess very few or zero moons.

core_concepts.title: Jovian (Outer) Planets
core_concepts.description: The last 4 planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) are called 'Outer or Jovian' (Jupiter-like) planets. They are massive, composed primarily of gases (Hydrogen and Helium) and ice, and all of them have ring systems.

core_concepts.title: The Asteroid Belt
core_concepts.description: This is a massive ring of rocky debris and minor planets located exactly between the orbits of 'Mars' and 'Jupiter'. This belt acts as a physical boundary separating the inner rocky planets from the outer gaseous giants.

core_concepts.title: Chemical Composition of Earth (SIAL, SIMA, NIFE)
core_concepts.description: According to Austrian geologist Eduard Suess, the Earth is chemically divided into: 1. SIAL - The continental crust, rich in Silica (Si) and Aluminium (Al). 2. SIMA - The oceanic crust/upper mantle, rich in Silica (Si) and Magnesium (Ma). 3. NIFE - The Earth's core, composed of heavy metals like Nickel (Ni) and Iron (Fe - Ferrous).

important_entities.name: Ganymede
important_entities.key_fact: Largest Moon in the Solar System
important_entities.significance: Ganymede is a moon orbiting 'Jupiter'. It is so massive that it is actually larger than the planet Mercury. (For context, Saturn's largest moon is 'Titan', and Earth's only moon is 'Luna').

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The State of the Inner Core
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A highly conceptual trap: As we go deeper into the Earth, the temperature rises. The core is as hot as the surface of the Sun (approx. 6000°C). So why isn't it melted? Remember, the Earth's 'Outer Core' is liquid, but the 'Inner Core' is completely 'Solid' due to the extreme, unimaginable 'Pressure' keeping the atoms locked together.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The first two letters of these terms directly spell out the chemical elements that dominate that specific layer (Silica, Aluminium, Magnesium, Nickel, Iron).

exam_strategy_tips: Between which two planets is the Asteroid Belt located? This is an SSC and Railway favorite. Answer: 'Mars and Jupiter'.
If asked which planet has the lowest density, the answer is 'Saturn' (its density is less than water, meaning it could theoretically float in a giant bathtub).
